defaults.permitted_development: Across Shropshire, domestic heat pumps are usually easiest on the planning permission route when the unit stays compact, sits discreetly, and can show a clean noise and neighbour-amenity story under the English planning system. rules.height_rules: Bulky housings, stacked equipment or extra height and visual prominence can make a heat pump feel more like external plant than a modest domestic installation.
rules.depth_rules: Projection from the wall or building line matters because exposed units and screens can quickly look more intrusive than a tighter, building-hugging installation.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting and noise are usually the first planning pressure points for heat pumps across Shropshire, especially where the unit sits near neighbours or a quiet garden edge.
rules.roof_rules: Across Shropshire, the roof is not usually the main heat-pump lever, but roof-level equipment and exposed service runs are often more sensitive than a discreet installation set lower on the building or in the garden.
rules.materials_rules: Well-scaled screening and restrained finishes usually work better than oversized housings that create a second visual problem around the plant.
